newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-ZILE SAYS BUDGET ACCORDING TO PLAN.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-ZILE SAYS BUDGET ACCORDING TO PLAN.

text.p: Finance Minister Robert Zile said on Friday said that the 1997 budget was going more or less according to plan according to figures for the first half.
He said that VAT collection was lower than planned but spending by ministries was also under-shooting.
"The surplus of revenues in the first half of 1997 was 102.33 percent," he told a news conference.
The finance ministry said the surplus was 8.91 million lats by July 16, made up of 310.26 million lats income, 284.87 million lats spending and net loans of 16.48 million lats.
Zile said that VAT revenues were lower than planned in the first half but that they would rise.
"In the second half of 1997 the total sales turnover will increase and therefore VAT collection will increase," he said.
But he noted that VAT rules had to be changed as they were good neither for the state revenue service nor for businesses.
"The spending of all ministries is only 88.9 percent of planned spending because they are not using all the available resources," he added.
